title: Enterprise Onboarding + Escalation + Integration + QBR Playbook
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary

This consolidated playbook covers enterprise onboarding, integration checklist, escalation paths, known issues and workarounds, the support process, and quarterly business review (QBR) & health check templates. It's intended for Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), and Support Engineers running the account lifecycle from initial technical onboarding to ongoing QBRs and incident management.

Goals

- Reduce time-to-first-successful-call (TTFSC) for enterprise customers to <= 3 business days for basic integrations.
- Define clear, repeatable escalation paths with SLA expectations.
- Provide a standard agenda & metrics for QBRs and operational health checks.
- Surface common issues and documented workarounds to reduce time-to-resolution (TTR).

Audience and ownership

- Primary owners: customer-success (CSMs), eng-developer-experience (SEs) for integration work, eng-sre & eng-platform for operational runbooks.
- Secondary stakeholders: product, eng-serving-runtime, security-and-compliance.

Onboarding overview (high level)

1. Pre-boarding (Sales -> CSM handoff)
   - Deliverables from Sales: contract, committed models, Dedicated/Private deployment details, network requirements, desired SLOs, and initial point-of-contact list.
   - Validate: billing account, contract SKU, and access provisioning timeline.

2. Kickoff call (Day 0)
   - Attendees: CSM, SE, customer engineering lead, network/security contact, PM (optional).
   - Agenda: goals & success criteria, timeline, architecture review, security & compliance checklist, integration approach (hosted/dedicated/private), QBR cadence.
   - Output: shared success plan (Google Drive / Confluence page) with milestone dates.

3. Technical onboarding (Days 1-7)
   - Tasks: API key provisioning, network allowlist setup, test account creation, sample app walkthrough, run simple generation/embedding calls.
   - Acceptance criteria: successful test calls (p50 latency under target if committed), sample prompts validated, and telemetry collection enabled.

4. Pilot & validation (Week 2-6)
   - Run pilot traffic, verify model quality with customer prompt set, enable caching/batching recommendations, and tune rate limits/throughput.
   - Prepare a pilot report with cost/latency tradeoffs and suggested production configuration.

Integration checklist (detailed)

- Network & Security
  - Confirm network topology: hosted (public outbound), dedicated (VPC peering or IP allowlist), private (VPC & on-prem connector).
  - Required firewall/Egress rules: allow outbound to api.redwood.ai IP ranges and ports 443. Provide customer with current IP ranges and region endpoints.
  - TLS & certs: TLS 1.2+, validate root CA. For Private deployments, confirm KMS/HSM keys and rotation windows.

- Authentication & Secrets
  - Provision API keys with correct role-based scopes.
  - Recommend short-lived keys for service-to-service calls; rotate keys quarterly.
  - Example curl test (replace API_KEY and MODEL):

  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-1.1","input":"Say hello"}'

- Rate limits & quotas
  - Default hosted: 120 requests/minute per key (subject to plan).
  - Dedicated: align with reserved throughput commitments. Add SE to request quota increases.
  - Backoff strategy: on 429, exponential backoff starting at 100ms, capped at 60s.

- Observability & Logging
  - Ensure request tracing header (X-Request-ID) is passed for correlating logs.
  - Enable customer-side telemetry and share sample dashboards (Prometheus/Grafana) for request latency, error rate, and token usage.
  - Confirm access to Redwood Console dashboards and role-based permissions.

- Data & Compliance
  - Confirm data residency and retention expectations. For Private deployments capture audit-log configuration and KMS details.
  - Redaction: advise customers on PII in prompts and use of client-side redaction rules where necessary.

Escalation matrix & process

- Definitions
  - Sev 1 (Critical): Service down for customer (total outage or persistent 50%+ error rate for >15 minutes). Target initial response: 15 minutes.
  - Sev 2 (High): Significant degradation (errors or latency impacting core flows for >30 minutes). Target initial response: 1 hour.
  - Sev 3 (Medium): Functional but degraded or intermittent issues; non-urgent bugs. Target initial response: 4 business hours.
  - Sev 4 (Low): Documentation requests, feature asks, or minor UI issues. Target response: 2 business days.

- Contact points and hours
  - Support portal (primary): support.redwood.ai (submit ticket with logs and X-Request-ID).
  - For Sev 1 after-hours: on-call SRE (pager) - CSM should escalate via Slack #cs-sev1-alert and cc on-call.
  - SE / Solutions escalation: include SE on ticket when integration or quota changes are required.

- Escalation steps (numbered)
  1. Triage by Support Tier 1: validate reproducibility, collect logs (request-id, sample payloads), check status.redwood.ai and recent deploys.
  2. If confirmed Sev1/2 -> escalate to on-call SRE and notify CSM + SE.
  3. For deployment-specific issues (Dedicated/Private), open a low-latency bridge (Zoom or Slack huddle) with infra/ops owners.
  4. SRE performs mitigation (traffic reroute, autoscale adjustments, failover to fallback model).
  5. Post-incident: create incident review doc and action items assigned within 3 business days.

SLA & SLO expectations to communicate to customers

- Uptime: Hosted API target 99.95% monthly. Dedicated SLA options available in contract.
- Latency: 95th percentile generation latency targets defined per model; surface model-specific baselines during onboarding.
- Error budget: acceptable error rate baseline of <0.5% for production traffic; thresholds in Console trigger alerts.

Known issues & workarounds (common items)

- Issue: Elevated 429s during burst traffic
  - Symptom: Client receives 429 throttle errors during unexpected traffic spike.
  - Workarounds: Implement client-side rate limiting and jittered exponential backoff. For Dedicated customers, request temporary burst capacity.

- Issue: Slightly lower output quality after quantized model rollout
  - Symptom: Model outputs appear more terse or lose factuality after switching to a quantized variant.
  - Workarounds: Pin to previous model variant if degradation is critical. Run evals with customer prompt set and apply recommended quantization profile from eng-serving-runtime.

- Issue: Timeouts on long-generation requests
  - Symptom: Upstream proxies close connections before token stream finishes.
  - Workarounds: Increase client-side timeout to model max tokens * expected token time (recommendation table below), or enable streaming mode and reconnect/resume logic.

Support process & ticketing best practices

- Ticket template (to speed triage) - include:
  - Customer name & environment (hosted/dedicated/private)
  - API key id (partial, last 4 chars)
  - X-Request-ID(s) and timestamps
  - Model name & version, payload size (tokens in/out)
  - Error messages, HTTP status codes, and sample payloads
  - Recent deploy ID or config change (if known)

- Escalation SLAs inside org
  - T1 resolves or escalates within 30 minutes for Sev1; 60 minutes for Sev2.
  - SRE tack action and mitigation within 2 hours for Sev1.
  - Postmortem published (internal) within 48 hours for Sev1; external incident summary to customer within 72 hours.

QBR & Health check cadence and templates

- Cadence
  - Initial QBR at end of pilot (Week 6).
  - Recurring QBRs: quarterly for enterprise accounts; monthly for high-velocity pilots.

- QBR agenda (standard)
  1. Roll call & objectives recap (5m)
  2. Business outcomes & usage highlights (10m)
  3. Performance & reliability review (latency, error rate, throughput) (15m)
  4. Cost & efficiency (tokens, amortized cost per request, recommendations) (10m)
  5. Quality and regression checks (prompt-set evaluations, model changes) (15m)
  6. Roadmap & requests (product features, model onboarding) (10m)
  7. Action items and timeline (5m)

- Health check dashboard (minimum metrics to share)
  - Avg / P95 latency per model
  - Error rate by endpoint and model
  - Token consumption by route and cost estimate
  - Cache hit ratio and batching efficiency
  - Recent deploys and incidents in period

Operational tables & quick references

- Timeout recommendation table:
  | Max tokens | Expected token time (ms/token) | Recommended timeout (ms) |
  |------------|-------------------------------|-------------------------|
  | 256        | 10                            | 4000                    |
  | 1024       | 12                            | 15000                   |
  | 4096       | 15                            | 65000                   |

- Common contact list:
  | Role | Team | Primary contact | Escalation channel |
  |------|------|-----------------|---------------------|
  | CSM (primary) | customer-success | asha.patel@redwood.ai | Slack: @asha_patel |
  | SE Lead | eng-developer-experience | javier.morales@redwood.ai | PagerDuty |
  | On-call SRE | eng-sre | see on-call rota | PagerDuty / Slack #sre-oncall |

Post-incident & continuous improvement

- Post-incident checklist:
  1. Create incident review page (link from ticket).
  2. Identify root cause (within 24 hours).
  3. Assign action items with owners and ETA (tracked in Jira).
  4. Validate fix in staging and schedule production rollout.
  5. Update playbook / known-issues list if new mitigation discovered.

Appendices

A. Sample onboarding timeline (Gantt style, simplified)
- Week 0: Sales handoff + kickoff
- Week 1: Network & auth + test calls
- Week 2-4: Pilot traffic + tuning
- Week 6: Pilot QBR & production cutover

B. Useful links
- Support portal: https://support.redwood.ai
- Status page: https://status.redwood.ai
- Console & dashboards: https://console.redwood.ai
- On-call rota & PagerDuty: internal link (see eng-sre runbook)
